rationale: B wins because it gives cleaner desk-by-desk stories and makes the missing proof explicit instead of laundering it into the premise. Its "Monzo's second US attempt starts invite-only, without the banking license it failed to get last time" is a real banking-trade angle; A's "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" smuggles in a tidy competitor map the update never supplied. B still overreaches in places, but its strategic spine is stronger and less blast-shaped.
gaps_in_A: "Monzo re-enters a US challenger-bank market that already has three incumbents" is the serious miss: neither "three incumbents" nor "Chime, Varo, Current" appears in the update.
"Monzo is explicitly pairing its first-ever annual profit with a second US run" overstates the record; the update gives same-window facts, not an explicit strategy.
"profitability is now a precondition for US expansion" tries to make a category trend from one company before bringing the comparative neobank evidence it admits it needs.
It misses the clean consumer-access angle in "invite-only at first"; that belongs as its own reader-facing story, not buried inside the competitor angle.
gaps_in_B: "then immediately spent it on the market that beat it once" is too certain; the update does not say the UK profit funded the US launch or that the spend timing is immediate.
"Nine million UK customers, zero in the US" invents the US customer count; invite-only does not equal zero.
"road to IPO" drags in a capital-markets storyline the update never supplied.
"renting a partner bank's charter" is useful shorthand, but the actual partner-bank legal and economic structure has to be nailed before that line leaves the building.
